note_on_method: Two kinds of claim appear below and they are kept apart deliberately. Claims about the world (how many courts a park has, whether a court is dedicated or dual-striped, what the tennis centre charges) come from the City of Long Beach and are cited. Claims about coverage are facts about this dataset rather than about Los Angeles County, and are worded so a reader cannot mistake one for the other.

slots.coverage:
One city in Los Angeles County is published here: Long Beach, with eight venues and forty-eight courts verified against the City's own pages, twenty-three of them dedicated to pickleball on the City's per-venue wording. Long Beach is the third California city on this site and the first in this county. The County also holds the City of Los Angeles, Pasadena, Torrance, Santa Monica and many other municipalities, as well as parks run by the County itself. None of those has been read against a named source, so none appears here.

Within Long Beach three City sites are named and not published. Somerset Park has a stated count, "Dual striping 8 pickleball on 2 tennis courts", at an address, "1500 E. Carson", that the Census geocoder places in the neighbouring city of Carson. The Billie Jean King Tennis Center is credited with four shared-use courts on the City's pickleball page and "8 Pickleball Courts, Fully Lighted" on its own. Whaley Park's line carries no number at all.
slots.distribution:
What is verified sits inside one city, and inside that city it splits on a fact the operator states on every line: whether a court is dedicated to pickleball or shared with something else. Twenty-three of the forty-eight are dedicated: eight at DeForest Park, four each at Silverado, Veterans and Marina Vista, two at Junipero Beach and one at Bayshore. The other twenty-five are eight lines on one tennis court at Veterans, four dual-striped courts "for either tennis or pickleball" at Marina Vista, two dual-striped at Bayshore, three "on a shared sports court" at El Dorado Park West and eight "shared-use" courts at the El Dorado Park Tennis & Pickleball Center. Veterans Park is the largest venue by count at twelve.

Everything else a county page could sort by is thin. Lighting is stated at one venue, the tennis centre, "8 Pickleball Courts, Fully Lighted", and the other seven carry no lighting answer either way. Price is stated at that same venue and nowhere else. Hours are stated at two: "Dawn to Dusk" at DeForest, and 7 a.m. to 9:30 p.m. on weekdays at the tennis centre. Indoor or outdoor is stated nowhere.
slots.gaps:
This is a Long Beach page under a county heading, and nothing here estimates the rest of the county. The City of Los Angeles, Pasadena, Torrance and Santa Monica have not been read, nor have the County's own parks, nor Cerritos and Lakewood. A city publishes here once three of its venues carry a named source and a date.

Inside Long Beach the gaps are of three kinds. One is a boundary: Somerset Park is a City of Long Beach park at an address the Census places in Carson, and it will publish the day that address resolves inside Long Beach. One is contradiction: the Billie Jean King Tennis Center's four courts on one City page and eight on another, and the City's own total of "24 dedicated pickleball courts" against a list that adds to twenty-three. One is silence: no surface, no nets, no indoor-or-outdoor word, no price at any park, and lighting at one venue in eight. Clubs, schools and commercial venues may hold courts across the county, and none of them publishes a source these pages have read.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts are there in Los Angeles County?
faqs.a: No honest page can tell you. What has been checked is 48 courts across eight venues, all in Long Beach, each with a source and a date you can see. The City of Long Beach itself names three more sites that cannot be published, and every other municipality in the county is unread.

faqs.q: Why is only Long Beach listed?
faqs.a: It is the only municipality in the county whose courts have been confirmed against a named source. A city appears here once three or more of its venues carry a source_url and a date_checked. Los Angeles, Pasadena, Torrance, Santa Monica and the County's own parks have not been read.

One: the El Dorado Park Tennis & Pickleball Center, "8 Pickleball Courts, Fully Lighted", open until 9:30 p.m. on weekdays. The other seven Long Beach venues carry no lighting answer either way, and they are recorded as unverified rather than as unlit.

faqs.q: Are any of the courts free?
faqs.a: The City does not say so, and no page here assumes it. Its park courts are first come, first served, which is a play format; the one stated price is at the tennis centre, $5 per person for drop-in play and $10 per court per hour to reserve.

Studebaker Rd.) - 3 pickleball courts on a shared sports court."; "Junipero Beach (2100 E. Ocean Blvd.) - 2 dedicated pickleball courts on repurposed half basketball court."; "Marina Vista Park (Colorado St. & Santiago) - Hybrid location: 4 dedicated pickleball courts and 4 dual-striped courts for either tennis or pickleball."; "Silverado Park (1545 W. 31st St.) - 4 dedicated pickleball courts. Call 562.570.1675."; "Somerset Park (1500 E. Carson) - Dual striping 8 pickleball on 2 tennis courts."; "Veterans Park (101 E. 28th St.) - Hybrid location: 8 pickleball courts on 1 tennis court and 4 dedicated pickleball courts."; "Whaley Park (5620 Atherton St.) - Dual-striped pickleball and volleyball court." Under "Long Beach Tennis Centers:": "Billie Jean King Tennis Center offers four shared-use pickleball courts"; "El Dorado Tennis Center offers eight shared-use pickleball courts"; "The pay-to-play rates at both tennis facilities are $5 per person for drop-in play (up to three hours), while private pickleball court reservations are $10 per court per hour." sources.evidence: Six published addresses matched at house-number level through the Census address file and were placed in Los Angeles County, CA (FIPS 06037) and the incorporated place "Long Beach city". Two - "5355 Eliot St." and "2800 Studebaker Road" - resolved through OpenStreetMap because the Census added a compass direction the City does not write, and were placed in Los Angeles County. "1500 E. Carson", the address the City publishes for Somerset Park, is placed by the Census in "Carson city", postcode 90745. Snapshot: data/sources/long-beach-county-census.json
